title: trace() output does not appear in the Output panel (AVM1 trace suppressed by INFO filter)
description:
USER-REPORTED BUG. Adding trace("message") to a frame script and running Test Movie leaves the Output pane empty (only the placeholder text shows). trace() never reaches the panel.

## Repro
1. New doc; on frame 1 add frame script: trace("hello");
2. Control > Test Movie (or the in-app Ruffle preview).
3. Bottom dock auto-switches to the Output tab (Shell handleTestMovie, useExportHandlers.ts:208) but stays empty: only "(Output from trace() statements will appear here during Test Movie.)".

## Path trace (compile -> run -> capture -> output)
- COMPILE (OK): AS2 trace("x") compiles to ActionTrace 0x26 correctly. packages/swf/src/actions.ts:56 ACTION_TRACE = actionNoArg(0x26); proven by packages/swf/src/__tests__/framescript.test.ts:174-183. Not a compile-side drop.
- RUN (OK): editor Test Movie -> useExportHandlers.ts handleTestMovie -> testMovie() bytes -> PlayerWindow -> packages/player/src/RufflePlayer.tsx createAndLoad, loads SWF via Ruffle with logLevel:'info', autoplay:'on'.
- CAPTURE (BROKEN): RufflePlayer.tsx:176-186 monkeypatches console.log/console.warn and forwards each call through shouldSuppressRuffleLog() before invoking onTrace. The capture assumes AS2 trace() arrives as a PLAIN console.log (see the unit-test assumption packages/player/src/__tests__/ruffleLogFilter.test.ts:46 "forwards plain AS2 trace() output" with input ["hello from trace()"]). It does NOT. In Ruffle, trace() goes through WebLogBackend::avm_trace (ruffle/web/src/log_adapter.rs:17-22) as tracing::info!(target:"avm_trace", ...). The WASMLayer (tracing-wasm 0.2.1, ruffle/web/src/lib.rs:1372 set_max_level INFO) formats that as a STYLED %c INFO message, so the console.log args look like ["%cINFO%c ... avm_trace ... hello", "color:..."]. After stripConsoleCssFormat() the line starts with "INFO".
- OUTPUT (OK but never fed): packages/authoring-ui/src/OutputPanel.tsx renders the messages[] prop fed by outputMessages state (Shell.tsx:3466-3469); handleTrace (useExportHandlers.ts:234) appends each onTrace line. This works -- it just never receives a trace line.

## ROOT CAUSE (file:line)
packages/player/src/ruffleLogFilter.ts:58-71 shouldSuppressRuffleLog(): RUFFLE_SUPPRESSED_PREFIXES (line 11-18) contains "info" and "avm". Ruffle's avm_trace is emitted as an INFO-level tracing event (log_adapter.rs:18), which the WASMLayer renders as a %cINFO%c line; after CSS stripping the text starts with "INFO" -> matches the "info" prefix -> SUPPRESSED at ruffleLogFilter.ts:71. So every trace() line is dropped before reaching onTrace/handleTrace, and the Output panel stays empty. Architecturally, the whole console.log-capture approach is the wrong path: Ruffle exposes a dedicated, reliable traceObserver callback (player element setter -> set_trace_observer, ruffle/web/src/lib.rs:494-496; available in the bundled build -- grep traceObserver/set_trace_observer in apps/desktop/public/ruffle/*.js) which fires ONLY for real avm_trace messages and is never used anywhere in the codebase (grep traceObserver in packages/apps = 0 hits).

## Regression vs never-worked
NEVER WORKED. The console.log interception + the suppressed "info"/"avm" prefixes were both present in the very first implementation, feat(0738) commit e64d986 (its message literally lists 'debug/warn/error/avm/info prefixes' as filtered). traceObserver was never wired. The recent OutputPanel re-theme (HEAD 149be189fae012f489e0eca49255c5c764144f0d batch) only changed styling/tokens, NOT the data path, so it is not the cause. Reference HEAD at investigation: 149be189fae012f489e0eca49255c5c764144f0d.

## Fix direction
Stop relying on console.log scraping for trace(). Register Ruffle's dedicated trace observer in RufflePlayer.tsx after the player loads: set player.traceObserver = (msg) => onTraceRef.current?.(msg) (the <ruffle-player> element exposes the traceObserver setter; bundled build supports set_trace_observer). Push those lines straight into the output store that OutputPanel reads (outputMessages via handleTrace). Keep the console.warn ERROR/WARN forwarding for diagnostics, but do NOT route avm_trace through the INFO-suppressing filter. (Alternatively, if console scraping must stay, stop suppressing the avm_trace INFO line specifically -- but the observer is the correct, less brittle path.)

## Acceptance
E2E (apps/desktop/e2e) that publishes/loads a SWF whose frame 1 has trace("hello") and asserts the line "hello" appears in the Output panel (data-testid="output-panel-messages" in OutputPanel.tsx) within the Test Movie flow. Plus a unit test that the trace path is fed by the observer, not the INFO-filtered console route.

## Related (distinct)
Task 1120 covers JSFL fl.trace()/fl.outputPanel.trace() not reaching the Output panel -- a different source path (jsfl/runtime.ts state.traces). This task is specifically the AS2/AVM1 runtime trace() path.
